Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation  $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=-\frac{4}{3},$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$   are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,x≈$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{3}{4})={(-48.590\,377…)}^{∘}≈-{48.5904}^{∘}
$$

This value is outside the required domain. To get a value inside the range, we add ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
{x}_{1}=-{48.5904}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={311.4096}^{∘}
$$

So,  our first solution is ${x}_{1}={311.4096}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={48.5904}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={48.5904}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978818/assets/d319d2ea403460a3b4d86c837a560fd5188476c425399145bb911e1414b0a6f5.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{48.5904}^{∘} \\  & ≈{228.5904}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈{228.6}^{∘},\,x≈{311.4}^{∘}.
$$
